title: Is Trakkr Worth It for Small Business?
metaTitle: Is Trakkr Worth It for Small Business?
metaDescription: Trakkr starts at $79/mo with a 14-day trial — and reviews call it steep for small budgets. Here's when it's worth it, plus a free way to check AI
primaryKeyword: is Trakkr worth it for small business
shortAnswer: Trakkr is worth it for a small business if you need ongoing, agency-grade tracking of how AI engines describe your brand and you can commit to at least $79/month after a 14-day trial. For a solo founder or budget-tight SMB that just wants to know whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini recommend them, a recurring subscription is often more than the job requires — and reviewers do flag Trakkr as "steep for small businesses." Run a free instant check first, then pay for monitoring only if the results show a problem worth tracking.
intro:
Trakkr is a capable AI visibility platform: it tracks how generative engines like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok describe, cite, and recommend your brand — daily, across all of its plans. The product is genuinely good at what it does. The real question for a small business isn't quality; it's whether the recurring cost matches what you actually need right now.

This page answers that honestly. We'll lay out Trakkr's real pricing, what reviewers say about it for smaller budgets, when it's clearly worth paying for, and a free way to get your first read before you commit to any subscription.

sections.heading: What Trakkr actually costs
sections.body:
Trakkr's published plans start at **Growth — $79/month** (about $790/year on annual billing) for one brand with daily tracking across roughly eight AI models, plus citation tracking, Reddit intelligence, and agent recommendations. The next tier, **Scale, is ~$399/month** for ~10 brands, unlimited team seats, and API access — that's the plan agencies and multi-brand teams gravitate to. Enterprise is custom-priced.

There's a **14-day free trial** with full Growth features and no card required, so you can evaluate before paying. But once the trial ends, ongoing use means a recurring $79+/month commitment — there is no open free-forever tier for continuous monitoring on the canonical pricing page. That distinction matters for a small business: the trial answers "what does this look like," not "can I keep watching this for free."

So the entry point for *sustained* monitoring is $79/month, and the fuller, multi-brand value really lives in the $399/month Scale tier.

sections.heading: What reviewers say about Trakkr for small budgets
sections.body:
Independent reviews are consistent on one point: Trakkr is a strong, specialized tool, but the price can pinch smaller operations. One review states plainly that "small businesses with limited budgets might find Trakkr expensive" and lists "steep pricing for small businesses" as a con. The same reviews note that the deep, AI-specific features are genuinely not found in general SEO tools — so you're paying a premium for focus, not fluff.

The other recurring caveat is that Trakkr **rewards active use**. Reviewers point out it "requires active strategy and resources to extract value." A monitoring subscription only pays off if someone on your side actually reads the reports, acts on the recommendations, and adjusts content over time. For a one-person business with no time budgeted for that work, a $79/month tool can quietly become shelfware.

None of this means Trakkr is overpriced — it means the value is real but conditional on commitment and follow-through.

sections.heading: When Trakkr is worth it — and when it isn't
sections.body:
**It's worth it if:** AI recommendations plausibly drive real revenue in your category (think B2B SaaS, professional services, local high-ticket services), you want *daily* trend data over time, you manage more than one brand or client, or you have someone who will act on the insights weekly. In those cases the $79–$399/month buys an early-warning system for your AI reputation, and reviewers agree it can "pay for itself" when AI traffic matters.

**It's probably overkill if:** you're a solo founder or early SMB who mainly needs to *find out* whether AI engines mention and recommend you, you don't yet have a content workflow to respond to findings, or your budget is tight enough that a fixed $79/month is a real decision. A one-time or occasional check, not a standing subscription, fits that situation better.

The trap to avoid is paying monthly for monitoring before you've confirmed there's a problem worth monitoring. Establish the baseline first.

sections.heading: Check your AI visibility free before you subscribe — try AEOeye

That's a different job than Trakkr's. AEOeye is built to give a non-expert a clear first read for free, no sales call and no card. It's newer and intentionally lighter on enterprise analytics and long-term historical dashboards than Trakkr — if you need daily tracking, multi-brand management, and trend history over months, Trakkr (or a tool like it) is the better fit, and we'd say so.

The sensible path for most small businesses: **run the free AEOeye audit first.** If it shows you're invisible or losing to competitors in AI answers, *then* a paid monitoring subscription like Trakkr's Growth plan is a justified next step.
